measures.title: Immigration inflow
measures.question: How many people arrived in this country in one year?
measures.scope: Countries that report immigration to Eurostat — EU27, EFTA and candidates.
measures.note: Eurostat counts anyone establishing residence for twelve months or more, including a country’s own citizens returning home. The bilateral model estimates flows between countries and has no separate notion of a returning national. The narrower Eurostat series, foreign and stateless citizens only, is shown alongside so that part of the gap can be read off directly rather than argued about.

series.label: Eurostat, all citizenships
series.method: Administrative and register counts submitted by national statistical institutes under Regulation (EC) 862/2007.

series.label: Eurostat, foreign and stateless only
series.method: Same collection, excluding arrivals holding the reporting country’s own citizenship.

series.label: Gaskin & Abel, modelled flow
series.method: Recurrent network over 18 covariates, trained to reproduce bilateral flows; total inflow here is the sum over all origins.

measures.title: Corridor flow, 2015–2020
measures.question: How many people moved along one origin–destination corridor?
measures.scope: Every corridor for which both models publish an estimate.
measures.note: Neither series is an observation. Both are statistical reconstructions of flows that no country measures bilaterally, built from successive migrant-stock tables by different estimators. This pair is the honest floor on how much of the migration picture is inference.

series.label: Gaskin & Abel
series.method: Deep recurrent network over 18 covariates, annual, 230 countries.

series.label: Abel, closed demographic accounting
series.method: Demographic accounting estimator da_pb_closed on quinquennial stock tables, summed over sex and over the disjoint outward, return and transit components.

measures.title: Foreign-born population
measures.question: How many people living here were born somewhere else?
measures.scope: Every country both sources cover at the 2020 stock anchor.
measures.note: These are not two independent measurements. The World Bank republishes UN DESA’s migrant-stock estimates, and the flow model is trained to reproduce the same UN DESA bilateral tables — so one is a model of the other’s source. What the gap measures is how much of the model’s stock is imputed across corridors UN DESA never observed. The anchor year 2020 is used rather than the model’s newest 2024 because it is the newest year both carry; comparing 2024 against 2020 would report four years of real migration as a disagreement between producers.

series.label: World Bank WDI, UN DESA estimates
series.method: SM.POP.TOTL — UN DESA quinquennial migrant-stock estimates, republished by the World Bank.

series.label: Gaskin & Abel, summed over origins
series.method: The destination margin of the model’s own bilateral stock matrix, summed across all 53,130 corridors before any trimming.

measures.title: Unemployment rate
measures.question: What share of the labour force is out of work?
measures.scope: All countries each source covers; the pairs run over the overlap.
measures.note: The World Bank series is labelled by its publisher as a modelled ILO estimate, not national reporting. Eurostat publishes the harmonised Labour Force Survey rate for its own members. The IMF publishes what member authorities report to it. Three producers, three routes to the same number.

series.label: World Bank, modelled ILO estimate
series.method: SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS — ILO harmonised model over national inputs.

series.label: Eurostat, Labour Force Survey
series.method: une_rt_a, ages 15–74, annual average of the harmonised LFS.

series.label: IMF, World Economic Outlook
series.method: LUR — as reported by member authorities to the WEO; recent years may be staff estimates rather than outturns.

measures.title: GDP per capita, PPP
measures.question: What is one person’s share of output, adjusted for what it buys locally?
measures.note: Both series are in current international dollars on the 2021 ICP round, so this is as close to like-for-like as two independent producers get. Comparing either against a constant-price series instead would open a gap of about ten percent that has nothing to do with disagreement — which is precisely the trap this view exists to expose.

series.label: World Bank WDI
series.method: NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD — national accounts compiled by the World Bank, ICP conversion factors.

series.label: IMF, World Economic Outlook
series.method: PPPPC — WEO database, current prices, PPP international dollars.

measures.title: Population
measures.question: How many people live here?
measures.note: The simplest quantity in the app, and the one where two agencies should have least room to differ. Whatever gap survives here is the floor under every per-capita figure elsewhere in Exodus, because every one of them divides by this.

series.label: IMF, World Economic Outlook
series.method: LP — WEO population in millions, rescaled here to people.
